method: Complete reads of five pinned test files; each Git blob identity and SHA256 checked. Executed original AST-extracted interpreter helper with a synthetic subprocess object; no generated scripts or upstream tests executed.
findings: JSON test uses filenames with control characters, quote and backslash and opens returned paths. It does not assert returned path set equals the two authored paths; both fixtures have equal size, so swapped or repeated paths can satisfy these assertions.

CSV test uses csv.DictReader and asserts complete ordered type/name/size rows including apostrophe/comma filename. Its nonzero-checksum assertion also accepts empty strings because set(empty) differs from the singleton zero set. A separate regression explicitly expects empty checksums for unhashed unique files.

Multi-formatter smoke test explicitly does not validate results. Summary/fdupes regression excludes directory rows and checks one suspicious item text, but does not assert full duplicate path partition.
Backup tests preserve /dev/null and its symlink from renaming; missing/non-character device returns without a recorded pytest skip.

Python formatter tests execute generated deletion scripts in upstream bodies, check content/size/inode safeguards and rerun stability. None executed here. Interpreter helper uses subprocess.call without checking its returncode; CalledProcessError is not raised merely by nonzero call result.

executed_control.scope: Original helper, stubbed subprocess.call, no interpreter process or generated cleanup script execution

limits: Source-level assertions and isolated helper control do not prove formatter runtime correctness.
No production optimization or complete repository-review claim.
